summary: The note describes the County of Gorizia, which remained an Imperial State of the Holy Roman Empire under the Inner Austrian Archdukes and was governed by a capitano. It covered the Isonzo Valley, Cormons, Duino and the former Venetian fortress of Gradisca. The note traces its territorial changes, including the 1647 separation of the Principality of Gradisca and the 1747 merger into the Princely County of Gorizia and Gradisca, a Habsburg crown land.
one_line: Gorizia's history as an Imperial State of the Holy Roman Empire and its 1647 and 1747 territorial changes into a Habsburg crown land.
key_facts: The inner county of Gorizia remained an Imperial State of the Holy Roman Empire while the Lienz area was administered with the Tyrolean crown land.
The inner county of Gorizia was ruled by the Inner Austrian Archdukes as part of the Austrian Circle.
The inner county of Gorizia was governed by a "capitano".
The territory of the County of Gorizia included the Isonzo Valley down to Aquileia.
The territory of the County of Gorizia included the area of Cormons and Duino.
The territory of the County of Gorizia included the former Venetian fortress of Gradisca, which was conquered by Imperial troops in 1511.
Monfalcone formed a Venetian exclave in the County of Gorizia from 1420 to 1797.
In 1647 Emperor Ferdinand III separated the "Principality of Gradisca" from Gorizia for his courtier Johann Anton von Eggenberg.
In 1747 the Principality of Gradisca and Gorizia were again merged to form the Princely County of Gorizia and Gradisca.
The Princely County of Gorizia and Gradisca was a crown land of the Habsburg Monarchy.
